pull_request.title: feat(home-speaker): a tool for the Vitruvian app, beside the app
pull_request.body:
Stage F of issue #3130, Tasks 8 and 9 (plan: PR #3190), pull request D: HomeSpeaker's tool for the Vitruvian app. Nothing of the Vitruvian app changes here. Needs SDK 1.1.0 for the kit's waker, which is released.

## What this does

- **The tool lives beside HomeSpeaker**, in `apps/desktop/home-speaker`, MIT: it drives HomeSpeaker's own program and reads the shared config file; English words; no preferences of its own. Five commands (say the clipboard, mute, volume, pick the speaker, broadcasting), an island page and a Settings panel. With HomeSpeaker absent or quit it says so and refuses.
- **Release:** HomeSpeaker's own release attaches `HomeSpeaker-X.Y.Z-tool.zip` with its `.sha256` (it has no mirror; the catalogue takes any VitruvianSoftware release). `zip-tool.sh` refuses a zip whose manifest version is not the release's.
- **CI:** the macOS lane names the tool's four tests.

## Checked on the final tree, after merging main

`HomeSpeakerToolTests` (19), `tool_conformance_test` (the built tool validates; `sayClipboard: refused, HomeSpeaker is not installed`; a panel of 3 blocks), `tool_version_test`, `zip_tool_test`; `swift package resolve` now finds the kit at 1.1.0; conformance check 430 ok, 0 fail; actionlint; licence verify; `//:tidy`. Planted regressions each failed their test and were reversed (the program seam ignored, so the test would have driven this Mac's HomeSpeaker; the asset renamed). No test reaches this Mac's HomeSpeaker, its config or the home folder: a scratch home, the `HOMESPEAKER_PROGRAM` seam, and `block-network`.

## Known, not from this change

Bazel's `//apps/desktop/home-speaker:HomeSpeakerTests` fails on main (it reads sources by path; CI does not run it).

feat(vitruvian-sdk): a tool can hand work to its thread from another

The kit gains ToolWaker: tool.waker.later takes work from any thread,
a window's or a child process's, and runs it on the kit's thread as soon
as it is between messages, after the hello, never while a handler runs or
waits for the app. The wire polls a wake pipe beside standard input; an
error the handed work throws goes to the tool's log. The guide says so
and the site's copy is synced. Stage F, Task 1 of issue #3130.

feat(home-speaker): the release attaches the tool's zip

HomeSpeaker's own release in this repository zips the tool beside the app:
publish.sh writes HomeSpeaker-X.Y.Z-tool.zip through scripts/zip-tool.sh,
the manifest at the top and bin/tool under it, named so the shared packaging
helper checksums and uploads it with the app's artifacts. zip_tool_test holds
the zip's contents, its name and the version the script refuses; ci.yaml's
macOS lane names the tool's four manual tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(home-speaker): the tool's zip lands in a dist folder given as ./dist

publish.sh passes the dist folder as ./dist. zip-tool.sh makes the zip
from inside its staging folder, so the relative path named a file there:
"Could not create output file", and the macOS build of this pull request
failed. The folder is made whole before the zip is written; the test gave
only a whole path, and now gives ./dist from another folder too.

SwiftPM writes Package.resolved now that the package has a dependency; no
package here commits one, so it is ignored.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
